body: claimed: marcbritten · 2026-11-24T17:27Z · no branch (research) · plan: research - answer the open questions in comments, then propose the sub-issues

**Research findings** (claim of 2026-11-24 17:27Z)

Sources:
- CamCraft `main` `582981bfa`: code reading only. I did not build or run CamCraft for this.
- SolidCraft source at v0.48.1 (MIT OR Apache-2.0). The lines below are the same at `main` `ce88badf2`, except where a second line number is given.
- Runs with the released `solidcraft-cli` 0.48.1 in a scratch folder, on SolidCraft's own example `examples/bracket.json`.

**A correction to the issue text.** In the 0.26.0 run that the issue gives, the operations were on a linked OBJ model, not on a `.sc` model. The pick id is the same geometry hash for each format (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:880-900`). So a `.sc` model must act the same, but I did not run a pick on a `.sc` model.

**1. The order of the names**
- SolidCraft makes one name for each face of a body, in the face order of the body. `derive` refuses a history whose face count is not the face count of the body (`crates/doc/src/history_names.rs:101-128`).
- The face count of a body is the length of its record's face list (`crates/kernel/src/body.rs:2263`; `topology()` is the record itself, `body.rs:109-114`).
- The cache writes the record with no change. `encode_native_body` writes `body.record()`, and "a decoded body is the encoded one, number for number" (`crates/kernel/src/native.rs:1-2, 41-55`). The cache writes the names in that order (`crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs:251-252`; `:253-255` at `main`).
- CamCraft keeps the decoded record with no change (`StepSolid.record`, `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs:187-195`). `tri_face` is an index into `record.faces` of that same record (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:226-233`).
- Run: the bracket example, built and saved with 0.48.1. The 11 names in `cache/model.json` and the 11 faces from `model.faces` agree index for index, all with `exact: true`.
- So name `i` in `model.names[n].faces` is face `i` of the record that CamCraft meshes, and `tri_face` uses the same index. SolidCraft documents that the cache holds the names (`docs/design-container.md`, "Model cache"). It does not state this order in words; the order comes from its source.
- **The order changes between revisions.** Run: the bracket with `width` 60 mm, then 80 mm. The two files have the same 11 names, in a different order. So a pick must keep the name, not the index, and each file maps its own names to its own faces.
- The cache also keeps `info` for each face: `[aliases, bounds, verified, synonyms]`. `verified` appears to be the same flag as `exact` in `model.faces`; in the run, both were true for all faces. So CamCraft can ignore a name that is not verified, with no call to SolidCraft.

**2. Welded faces and the source face**
- The kernel knows the source face of each triangle: `MachiningMesh::tri_face`, "the record face of each triangle" (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:46`).
- The `.sc` import drops it. `push_facets` copies only the three corners (`crates/geometry/src/kernel_import.rs:13-26`), and `Triangle` has only `a`, `b` and `c` (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/mod.rs:224-228`).
- The feature graph already maps each facet to its welded face (`facet_face`, `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:473-479`). With a source-face index for each facet, each welded face gets the set of source names under it.
- A welded face over two source faces gets two names, and a pick keeps both. One source face under two welded faces gives the same name to both; a pick then finds two faces and must refuse (see 4).
- Not checked: what `Mesh::from_facets`, model repair and the facet budget do to the order of the facets between `push_facets` and the feature graph. Not tested: how often welding joins or splits source faces on real parts.

**3. Where the name goes**

The pick must keep its source name (or names) after the old file is replaced. So the name on the pick is an optional field in the project file. For the map from facets to names, I see two shapes. The choice is yours:
- **A. Keep only the name on the pick.** At pick time and at re-import, read the names from the linked `.sc` file again: its cache and `tri_face`. This is the smallest change to the project file. It depends on a mesh of the same file that gives the same facets. Not checked: whether the mesh is deterministic.
- **B. Keep the source index of each facet and the name table on the model**, in the project file. This is a larger change to the file, with no second read of the source.

An older reader drops the new fields, and the picks still work by their geometry id. Whether this needs a `PROJECT_VERSION` step is your decision; the loss is harmless, as in #2374.

**4. A name that is gone or split**
- Proposal: refuse, as today, and give the name, for example "Face 'F2:side:b' of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- SolidCraft names the pieces of a split face with a qualifier (`F2:top#[...]`), and keeps the names of merged faces as aliases. Its own rule: a reference to an alias "finds nothing". CamCraft can use the same rule and not guess.
- Names can also change between SolidCraft releases. Run: 0.48.1 opened `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc`, which SolidCraft 0.40.0-rc.2 saved with cache format 8, and evaluated it again. It refused the feature `Fillet5`, because a stored name "no longer exists as it was picked". The refusal covers this case too.

**5. Edges and chains**
- The cache keeps face names only. SolidCraft names an edge by the two faces it joins; for example, `F3:blend(F2:side:b|F2:side:c)` is the fillet face on that edge.
- Proposal: faces first. Edges and chains later, from the pair of face names.

**6. Fit with #3817 and #3814**
- All three read SolidCraft's published container through `crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/`. One reader of `cache/model.json` can serve them.
- With names, the change summary of #3814 (carried, added and missing faces) can name the faces.

**7. Tests**
- Fixtures: the bracket example at `width` 60 mm and 80 mm. I made both with `solidcraft-cli run <script> --save`: SolidCraft's `examples/bracket.json`, and the same script with the width changed. The two files have the same names in a different order.
- These fixtures are SolidCraft output. `testdata/models/` already holds `.sc` files that SolidCraft made, but your rule on SolidCraft material applies. A script of your own can make equal fixtures.
- Pins:
  - a pick on a side face survives the width change by its name;
  - a pick on a face that a change removes is refused, with its name;
  - a model with no names (STEP, OBJ, STL) and a name that is not verified behave as today.

**Proposed sub-issues** (each a need and a "Done means", not an implementation)
1. Import: a `.sc` model knows the source face and its name for each facet. No change in behaviour. Done means: after a `.sc` import, the source name of each facet is known; other formats have none.
2. Picks: a face pick on a `.sc` model keeps its source name, and finds its face again by that name when the model imports again. The geometry still decides. A missing, split or unverified name refuses as today, with the name. Done means: on the bracket fixtures, a pick survives 60 mm to 80 mm, and a pick on a removed face is refused by name.
3. MCP: `list_features` and `get_operation_geometry` show the face name. The change summary of #3814 names the faces.
4. Later (P8): edges and chains, by the names of the faces they join.

I can file these sub-issues next. Tell me if the direction is wrong.
Triage: `enhancement`, `P8`, `needs-research`, `effort:max`, `area:3d`. A research issue with a live claim by @marcbritten. Related: SolidCraft's `.sc` model format.
Consider the motion kernel rewrite. Check issues for correlation

claimed: marcbritten · 2026-11-26T18:55Z · no branch (research) · plan: research - findings refreshed at SolidCraft 0.50.0 and CamCraft 0.27.0, a `.sc` baseline run, a path kernel check; next, file the sub-issues

**Refresh of the findings, a baseline run, and the path kernel** (comment of 2026-11-24)

Sources:
- SolidCraft v0.50.0 and `main` `5568a0b673`;
- CamCraft v0.27.0, `main` `773736856` and `side/path-kernel` `cb93488c0`, code reading only;
- runs with the released `solidcraft-cli` 0.50.0 and the released `camcraft-cli` 0.27.0 (a headless MCP session), in a scratch folder. I did not build CamCraft.

**All code links hold.** Only line numbers moved:
- SolidCraft: `derive` at `crates/doc/src/history_names.rs:107-109`; `face_count` at `crates/kernel/src/body.rs:2436` (0.50.0) and `:2532` (`main`); the encoder at `crates/kernel/src/native.rs:42`; the name writer at `crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs:254-263`.
- CamCraft: no change at these lines. `face_id` at `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:884`, `facet_face` at `:477`, `tri_face` at `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:46`, `push_facets` at `crates/geometry/src/kernel_import.rs:13-26`, `Triangle` at `crates/geometry/src/geometry/mod.rs:224-228`. The import still drops `tri_face`, and the `.sc` reader still reads no names.
- SolidCraft 0.50.0 still writes `solidcraft-model-cache/10`, and CamCraft still reads formats 8 and 10 (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/mod.rs:53`).

**SolidCraft runs on 0.50.0:**
- The bracket example: the 11 cached names agree with `model.faces` index for index, all exact and verified.
- `width` 60 mm, then 80 mm: the same 11 names, in a different order.
- For the bracket (no Split Face), the names from 0.48.1 and from 0.50.0 are the same, in the same order, at both widths.
- `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (saved by 0.40.0-rc.2) still refuses the feature `Fillet5` on 0.50.0.

**Baseline on 0.27.0: picks on a `.sc` model after a design change**

This is the `.sc` run that my correction of 2026-11-24 said was missing. Released 0.27.0, no build, MCP only.
- Steps:
  1. Import the bracket at 60 mm as `part`. Add operations with face, patch and edge picks, and generate them. Six operations held a pick; the other picks were refused at pick time by the rules of their kind (for example, a 2D Pocket refuses a vertical face).
  2. Replace the file at the same path with the 80 mm revision. Import it again under the same name (`import_model`).
  3. Generate each operation again, and compare the `list_features` ids.
- The 11 SolidCraft faces became 6 flat faces and 3 patches (216 faces, 3 patches and 19 chains in all). One patch covers three SolidCraft faces that meet tangentially: `F2:side:b`, the fillet `F3:blend(F2:side:b|F2:side:c)` and `F2:side:c`.
- After 60 → 80 mm, by the `list_features` ids, the features of 8 of the 11 SolidCraft faces were lost: 5 flat faces and the three-name patch. Only `F2:start` and the two hole walls kept their ids.

  | Kind | Carried | Missing | Added |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Faces | 193 | 23 | 23 |
  | Patches | 2 | 1 | 1 |
  | Chains | 9 | 10 | 10 |

- The 80 mm file holds the same 11 names. So each of the 8 lost faces has its name in the new file.
- The model updated in place. Every operation went Stale, also the operations whose picks were kept.
- At generate, 4 of the 6 operations were refused, and 2 generated (a 2D Pocket on a hole wall, and a 2D Contour on a hole rim). The refusals:
  - the top face, and a flat face in the curved patch: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it";
  - the curved patch: "Curved face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it";
  - the end edge of the top face: "Edge of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- The messages do not say which face or edge.
- The `import_model` answer held only the facet count (2008, then 2276) and the "cached final body only" note. It held no change summary; #3814 asks for one.
- Not run: a design with Split Face (`former`), the window's file watcher, a reopened project.

**New in SolidCraft 0.50.0: new names for Split Face pieces, and `former`**
- Split Face now names each piece by the feature and its side of the tool, for example `…#[F7:split:in]` (commit `7533baabaa`, 2026-11-25). Before, a piece kept the name of the face it came from, told apart by the faces around it. So the names of Split Face pieces changed between 0.48.1 and 0.50.0.
- Each piece keeps its old name in a new, fifth `info` item: `[aliases, bounds, verified, synonyms, former]` (`crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs:254-260`). Other faces keep four items.
- SolidCraft finds a face by its `former` name: "a reference a design saved then holds finds this very face by it" (`crates/doc/src/history_names.rs:58-61`). The match is exact (`:768`).
- So a name can change between SolidCraft versions, and the file gives the bridge. Proposal for sub-issue 2: after a re-import, a face whose `former` is equal to the old name of a picked face counts as a face with that name, as in SolidCraft. If more than one face matches, refuse.
- A reader must accept `info` entries with four items and with five items.
- The bracket has no Split Face, so no run showed a `former` item.

**The path kernel (#4023)**

You asked me to consider the motion kernel rewrite. I read this as the path kernel, #4023. If you mean a different issue, tell me. What I found at `side/path-kernel` `cb93488c0`:
- K1 (#4025) turns each pick (an edge, a face, a chain, or points) into a `Chain`, and the chains into one region. Its decision record says: "No project file and no posted program changes" (`docs/decisions/4025-kernel-region.md` on the side branch).
- No code in `crates/pathkernel` or `crates/motion` uses the pick types (`GeoSel`, `FeatureSel`, `FaceId`) or the refusal "is no longer in the model". The kernel and its adapter take geometry, not pick ids.
- This work changes pick ids when the model imports again, before any pick is resolved. So it does not depend on which planner the switch selects. A pick that follows by name is a normal pick id, and the kernel needs no names.
- If pick resolution moves into the kernel adapter at the switch-over, the "no longer in the model" refusals move with it. This work keeps those refusals as they are.
- The start and exit picks (#3325 and its PRs) are coordinates, not feature ids (`crates/app/src/project/path_picks_dto.rs`). This work does not change them.
- Files: in `crates/app`, the side branch changes `lib.rs`, `operation/mod.rs`, `operation/planner_switch.rs` and `operation/generate/run_job.rs`. I expect no change in these files for this work. No open PR changes the `.sc` reader, the feature graph, `revision.rs` or `UpdateModel` (checked 2026-11-26).

**Tracking**

I track all the path kernel issues, and the other open issues and PRs that can change the code of this work. Before each claim, I check them for changes to the same files. If an open PR changes the same files, I stack on it or I wait for it. I report each new conflict in this issue.

**Sub-issue 2 has new words.** In my list of 2026-11-24, sub-issue 2 said that a pick "keeps its source name". The new text gives only the need: a pick follows its face by its SolidCraft name, and a pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report. Where the name is kept is part of the design.

Next, after your reply, I file the four sub-issues, with the questions for you in sub-issues 1 and 2. Tell me if the direction is wrong.

**Sub-issues filed**

- #4212 Import: keep the SolidCraft source face and its name for each facet of a `.sc` model. Questions Q4 (fixtures) and Q5 (cache format 10 only).
- #4213 Picks: a face pick follows its face by the SolidCraft name when the model imports again. Questions Q1 (`PROJECT_VERSION` step), Q2 (follow, or offer the follow) and Q3 (`Patch` picks).
- #4214 MCP: show the face names, and name the followed and lost picks after a re-import. It fits #3814.
- #4215 Picks: a chain pick follows by the pair of SolidCraft face names.

Each sub-issue gives the need and "Done means", not the code. I filed them before your reply on the path kernel. If the direction is wrong, I change them or close them.
